topic: SC: man kept in jail for 7 years, 3 months and 21 days after acquittal gets Rs 30 lakh (raised from Rs 2 lakh) - acquittal of 20 Jan 2018 never reached the jail, released 19 May 2025; egregious violation of Article 21; State of Chhattisgarh to pay in four weeks, Rs 5 lakh to savings and balance in fixed deposit under DLSA supervision; no law on compensation for wrongful imprisonment (Law Commission 277th Report); all High Courts to consider Madhya Pradesh-style safeguards and online Criminal Justice Ecosystem (Devilal Gond v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors., 2026 INSC 1226, 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1153, Justices Augustine George Masih and Sanjeev Sachdeva, 16 Nov 2026)

slides.title: Acquitted in 2018, **jailed till 2025**
slides.subtitle: The Supreme Court raised his compensation from Rs 2 lakh to **Rs 30 lakh**.
slides.cite: **Devilal Gond v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors.** · 2026 INSC 1226 · 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1153 · Justices Augustine George Masih and Sanjeev Sachdeva · 16 November 2026

slides.label: What happened
slides.title: Free on paper, **locked up** in fact
bullets: He got a life sentence for murder in 2013. The Chhattisgarh High Court **acquitted him on 20 January 2018**, and the State did not appeal.
News of the acquittal **never reached the jail**. A records check on 15 May 2025 found the lapse, and he was freed on **19 May 2025**.
He spent **7 years, 3 months and 21 days** in jail after acquittal, from about age 28 to about 35.

slides.label: What the Court said
slides.title: A **gap in communication** is no answer
bullets: Keeping him in jail after acquittal had **no authority of law** and was an egregious violation of **Article 21**.
The State blamed a gap between the jail and legal aid officials. The Court said this showed poor coordination and **institutional failure** by all authorities.
slides.note: **Law fact:** When the State violates a fundamental right, courts can order compensation. The State **cannot claim sovereign immunity** against it.

slides.label: The compensation
slides.title: From Rs 2 lakh to **Rs 30 lakh**
bullets: He had sought Rs 50 lakh; the High Court gave **Rs 2 lakh**. The Supreme Court ordered **Rs 30 lakh**, payable by the State within **four weeks**.
**Rs 5 lakh** goes to his savings account. The balance stays in a **fixed deposit**, with monthly interest paid to him.
Compensation must help a person **rebuild his life**. It cannot be a token amount.

slides.label: What comes next
slides.title: So this does not **happen again**
bullets: India has **no law** fixing compensation for wrongful imprisonment. The Court referred to the Law Commission's **277th Report**.

All High Courts must consider safeguards like Madhya Pradesh's: prompt communication of **release orders**, compliance reports, prison inspections and an **online system** linking courts, police and jails.

caption:
Acquitted in 2018, but still in jail until 2025 ⚖️⛓️

The Chhattisgarh High Court acquitted Devilal Gond of a murder charge on 20 January 2018, and the State did not appeal. But the news of his acquittal never reached the prison. He walked out only on 19 May 2025, after a records check found the lapse. By then he had spent 7 years, 3 months and 21 days in jail with no legal basis, from about age 28 to about age 35.

The High Court awarded him Rs 2 lakh. On 16 November 2026, the Supreme Court raised this to Rs 30 lakh, payable by the State within four weeks. The Court called the detention an egregious violation of the right to life and liberty under Article 21. The State blamed a communication gap between the jail and legal aid officials, but the Court said this showed poor coordination and institutional failure by all the authorities. Compensation, it said, must help a person rebuild his life and cannot be a token amount.

The Court also noted that India has no law setting out compensation for wrongful imprisonment, and referred to the Law Commission's 277th Report. All High Courts must now consider safeguards like those in Madhya Pradesh, including prompt communication of acquittal and release orders and an online system linking courts, police and prisons.

Case: Devilal Gond v. State of Chhattisgarh & Ors., 2026 INSC 1226, 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1153
Court: Supreme Court of India, Justices Augustine George Masih and Sanjeev Sachdeva, 16 November 2026
